newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans 8-year schooling opposed by Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans 8-year schooling opposed by Islamists.

text.p: Turkey has nearly completed an eight-year compulsory education plan that has sparked fresh tensions between the Islamist and conservative wings of government, Education Minister Mehmet Saglam said on Tuesday.
"Our preparatory work is continuing on introducing eight years' education in the coming school year," Saglam was quoted as saying by the state-run Anatolian news agency.

Turkish shares were down more than three percent in late trade on Tuesday, and brokers said concern about Islamist opposition to the plan from within Turkey's nine-month-old coalition were partly to blame.
Islamists believe the plan would threaten the future of religious schools, which produce many of their supporters.

The eight-year education proposal was among the measures put forward by the country's military-dominated National Security Council after a meeting last month that decided to clamp down on rising Islamist activism.
Members and supporters of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party fear the proposal would ultimately spell the end of Moslem Imam-Hatip schools.
Under existing laws, compulsory state education in Turkey lasts five years and schoolchildren can only then attend Imam-Hatip schools.
Saglam, from the True Path Party (DYP) of Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, said he would announce the new education plans when the work was completed.
